subject: maths
title: Prime factorisation and the Fundamental Theorem

goals: State the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic
Find the prime factors of a composite number
Find the HCF and LCM using prime factorisation

cards.title: Prime numbers and composites
cards.body:
A **prime number** is a number greater than 1 that has exactly two factors: 1 and itself. Examples are 2, 3, 5, 7.

A **composite number** is a number greater than 1 that has more than two factors. For example, 12 is composite because its factors are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12.
cards.remember: The number 1 is neither prime nor composite.

cards.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic
cards.body: The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic states that every integer greater than 1 can be written as a product of prime numbers, and this factorisation is unique up to the order of the factors. For example, 12 = 2 × 2 × 3, which is the same up to order as 2 × 3 × 2.
cards.remember: This theorem is the basis for finding HCF and LCM.

cards.question: Which of these is a prime number?
cards.why: 1 is neither prime nor composite. 9 = 3 × 3 and 12 = 2 × 2 × 3 are composite. 17 has no factors other than 1 and 17.

cards.title: How to find HCF and LCM
cards.remember: This relation holds only for two positive integers.

rows.value: Write the prime factors of both numbers. HCF is the product of the common prime factors raised to the lowest power.
Write the prime factors of both numbers. LCM is the product of all prime factors raised to the highest power.
For two numbers a and b: HCF × LCM = a × b

steps: Find HCF by taking common primes to the lowest power: 2 × 3 = 6
Find LCM by taking all primes to the highest power: 2² × 3² = 4 × 9 = 36
Check using the relation: HCF × LCM = 6 × 36 = 216 and 12 × 18 = 216
cards.question: Find the HCF and LCM of 12 and 18 using prime factorisation.
What is the prime factorisation of 45?
cards.why: 45 = 9 × 5 = 3² × 5. The choice with 5² × 3 equals 75, not 45, because the power of 5 is too high. 3 × 15 is not a prime factorisation because 15 = 3 × 5, and 45 on its own is not factorised at all.

cards.question: The prime factorisation of a number is 2³ × 3². What is the number?
cards.why: 2³ is 8 and 3² is 9. Multiplying them gives 8 × 9 = 72. 54 is 2 × 3³, which has a different prime factorisation.

points: Every integer greater than 1 has a unique prime factorisation up to order
Use common primes for HCF and highest powers for LCM
The product of the HCF and LCM of two numbers equals their product
